children: Grades broadly fell on Thursday, dealers said, as some supply concerns in the Middle East eased, though prices remained elevated.
Saudi Arabia was seeking to return about half the capacity of its East-West oil pipeline within days after the link was halted last week following drone attacks, Bloomberg reported.
The critical pipeline had allowed Saudi Arabia to circumvent the Strait of Hormuz by exporting some volumes via the Red Sea.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said a Togo-flagged oil tanker was struck while attempting to make an "illegal passage" through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, Iranian state media said.
The tanker came to a halt after catching fire, the Revolutionary Guards Navy added.
Light Louisiana Sweet for October delivery fell 88 cents to a midpoint of a $4.50 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $4.00 and $5.00 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
Mars Sour fell $3.75 to a midpoint of a $3.25 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $3.15 and $3.35 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
WTI Midland fell 10 cents to a midpoint of a $1.30 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $1.20 and $1.40 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
West Texas Sour was steady at a midpoint of a 20-cent discount and was seen bid and offered between a 70-cent and 50-cent a barrel discount to U.S. crude futures
WTI at East Houston, also known as MEH, traded between a $1.75 and $1.95 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
fell $1.01 to settle at $104.82 a barrel
futures fell 52 cents to settle at $101.91 a barrel
The Brent/WTI spread narrowed 78 cents to last trade at minus $7.54, after hitting a high of minus $6.72 and a low of minus $8.40
